items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ray Nance run out with his trumpet...

ctx.x: Well, they had Harry Carney. Anybody with Harry Carney, the saxophone section is going to sound different, because he was a great, GREAT baritone player. Big sound and everything. And Johnny Hodges, the way he played. It was a special band. You couldn’t... Duke

had picked them just right. He wrote his arrangements very compatible with the guys who were playing them. Ray Nance run out with his trumpet... It was a different kind of band. It wasn’t just a jazz band. See, critics got carried away hollering about a jazz band, but they played a whole lot more stuff than jazz.
You’ve been talking each of the alto saxophone players you liked—and I suppose on tenor and baritone, too—all having an individual sound, a stamp...
